assumptions: the range is ordered by the routine's own record comparison; the routine does not check ordering, so the search is meaningful only on such a range
the range pair at the caller stack slots is a begin/end pair for the same record array probed at both sites; the range's own provenance beyond the call setup is not pinned

consumers.argument_setup_pattern: at both sites rdi comes from stack slot 0xc0(rsp) and rsi from stack slot 0xc8(rsp), the same range pair; rdx is the record pointer under test
consumers.caller_loop: the caller walks its own 0x20-stride table, advancing rbx by 0x20 per iteration until it reaches the table end; at the first site it probes the range with the current record (rdx = rbx); a 0 result builds a derived record at rsp+0x290 through the call at 0x603db00 (rdi = derived slot, rsi = rbx) and probes again at the second site with rdx = that derived record; a nonzero result at the first site advances the loop without building anything

presence_tail.combined_meaning: the candidate is the first record not less than the key, so key-not-less-than-candidate together with candidate-not-less-than-key means equality; the routine therefore returns 1 exactly when an equal record is present
presence_tail.comparison: byte compare of key against candidate over min(key length, candidate length) via the same memcmp PLT, with the key as the first compare operand; on a tie, the length difference (key length - candidate length) decides, clamped: above 0x7fffffff counts as positive, below -0x80000000 counts as negative
presence_tail.result_rule: returns 1 exactly when the key is not less than the candidate (byte compare positive, or byte compare tied with key length >= candidate length), else 0

record_layout.other_fields: bytes at +0x10..+0x1f are never read by this routine; their roles are not claimed

arguments.rdi: begin pointer: first 0x20-byte record of the range
arguments.rdx: key record pointer (data pointer at +0x00, length at +0x08)
arguments.rsi: end pointer: one past the last 0x20-byte record of the range

routine.prologue: endbr64, pushes r15, r14, r13, r12, rbp, rbx, 0x28 stack reserve, no canary check
routine.result: eax is 1 when the range holds a record equal to the key, else 0; the sole caller tests al

search_loop.comparison: byte compare over min(candidate length, key length) via the memcmp PLT at 0x63f0aa0; on a tie, the length difference (candidate length - key length) decides, clamped to the int32 range: a difference at or above 0x80000000 counts as non-negative, a difference below -0x80000000 counts as negative
search_loop.count: count = (end - begin) >> 5, arithmetic shift; a count of 0 or less skips the loop and enters the presence tail
search_loop.exit: when the count reaches 0, the cursor is the first record not less than the key (the lower-bound candidate), or the end pointer
search_loop.halving: mid = count >> 1; the candidate record is begin + mid * 32
search_loop.lower_half: comparison non-negative (candidate >= key): cursor unchanged, count becomes mid
search_loop.upper_half: comparison negative (candidate < key): cursor moves to the record after the candidate, count becomes count - mid - 1

unknowns: behavior when end < begin (the negative count path still enters the presence tail, but no such call is observed)
what the derived-record construction at 0x603db00 computes from the current record
the caller's branches after the second probe (both outcomes leave the probed region; neither is traced here)
